sentences.en: From The New York Times, this is The Interview.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，这里是《访谈》栏目。

sentences.en: I'm Lulu Garcia-Navarro.
sentences.zh: 我是露露·加西亚-纳瓦罗。

sentences.en: Since the founding of our democracy, there's been a separation of powers.
sentences.zh: 自我们的民主制度建立以来，权力一直实行分立。

sentences.en: The Senate, in particular, was created to act as a stabilizing force with its own important responsibilities.
sentences.zh: 特别是参议院的创立，旨在扮演稳定力量的角色，并肩负着重要的自身职责。

sentences.en: But after almost a year of the second Trump presidency, during which time he's pursued an aggressive agenda, the Senate is arguably weaker than ever.
sentences.zh: 但在特朗普第二任期经历了近一年、期间他一直在推行激进议程之后，参议院可以说比以往任何时候都更加弱势。

sentences.en: With some critics and senators saying it is abandoning its role in checking presidential power.
sentences.zh: 一些批评人士和参议员表示，它正在放弃制衡总统权力的角色。

sentences.en: So today I'm having a different kind of conversation than we usually do on the show.
sentences.zh: 因此，今天我将进行一场与我们节目中通常不同的对话。

sentences.en: A roundtable about the state of the Senate with three lawmakers who all decided to leave it.
sentences.zh: 这是一场关于参议院现状的圆桌讨论，邀请了三位决定离开它的议员。

sentences.en: Jeff Flake, a Republican, represented Arizona and left office in 2019, warning that the influence of Trumpism on the GOP would be corrosive to his party.
sentences.zh: 杰夫·弗雷克是一名共和党人，曾代表亚利桑那州，并于2019年离任，他警告说特朗普主义对共和党的影响将侵蚀他的政党。

sentences.en: We must never regard as normal the regular and casual undermining of our democratic norms and ideals.
sentences.zh: 我们绝不能将经常性且随意破坏我们民主规范与理想的行为视为常态。

sentences.en: Joe Manchin represented West Virginia, first as a Democrat who frequently voted with Republicans, and later as a registered independent.
sentences.zh: 乔·曼琴曾代表西弗吉尼亚州，最初是一名经常投票支持共和党的民主党人，后来注册为无党派人士。

sentences.en: He left the Senate at the start of this year.
sentences.zh: 他在今年年初离开了参议院。

sentences.en: I was not elected to take a side.
sentences.zh: 我当选不是为了选边站。

sentences.en: I was elected to represent all sides.
sentences.zh: 我当选是为了代表所有各方。

sentences.en: And Tina Smith is a Democrat who currently represents Minnesota.
sentences.zh: 蒂娜·史密斯是一名目前代表明尼苏达州的民主党人。

sentences.en: And earlier this year announced that she won't be seeking re-election in 2026.
sentences.zh: 她于今年早些时候宣布不会在2026年竞选连任。

sentences.en: After 20 years of hard and rewarding work in the public sector,
sentences.zh: 在公共部门经历了20年艰辛而有回报的工作之后，

sentences.en: I'm ready to spend more time with my family.
sentences.zh: 我准备花更多时间陪伴家人。

sentences.en: I wanted to gather these three to get their read on the state of the Senate and our politics and democracy more broadly.
sentences.zh: 我想把这三位聚在一起，听听他们对参议院现状以及更广泛的政治和民主制度的看法。

sentences.en: So here's my conversation with Senators Flake, Manchin, and Smith.
sentences.zh: 以下是我与弗雷克、曼琴和史密斯三位参议员的对话。

sentences.en: I want to thank you all for being here.
sentences.zh: 我要感谢你们所有人的光临。

sentences.en: It is a great pleasure to have you here on this sort of gray winter day in Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 在这个华盛顿特区略显阴冷的冬日，很高兴能请到你们来到这里。

sentences.en: You are all three former or soon-to-be former senators, and you all left at different periods of the last 10 years.
sentences.zh: 你们三位都是前参议员或即将卸任的参议员，而且你们在过去10年的不同时期离职。

sentences.en: And I'm hoping, frankly, that because you are leaving or have left, you will feel a little bit more unleashed in being able to discuss your true feelings and thoughts.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我希望因为你们正在离开或已经离开，你们在表达真实感受和想法时会感到稍微更加无拘无束。

sentences.en: That's why we left.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们离开的原因。

sentences.en: So I want to start by asking you all to give me a word or a sentence, something brief, that describes the state you think the Senate is in right now.
sentences.zh: 所以我想首先请你们每个人用一个词或一句话，也就是简短的内容，来描述你们认为参议院目前处于什么状态。

sentences.en: And I want to start with you, Senator Smith, because you are actually sitting in said body.
sentences.zh: 我想从你开始，史密斯参议员，因为你实际上正身处这个机构之中。

sentences.en: Broken.
sentences.zh: 破碎的。

sentences.en: Senator Flake?
sentences.zh: 弗雷克参议员？

sentences.en: Probably retreat.
sentences.zh: 可能是退缩。

sentences.en: You know, in this system, presidency, just by virtue of the system, gains more power over time.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在这个体制中，仅凭体制本身的特点，总统就会随着时间获得更多权力。

sentences.en: But what's been frustrating is to see the Senate just willingly give up Article I authority.
sentences.zh: 但令人沮丧的是看到参议院竟然心甘情愿地放弃第一条赋予的权力。

sentences.en: Abdication.
sentences.zh: 抛弃职责。

sentences.en: They've abdicated basically responsibilities of what their purpose of being there.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上放弃了他们存在目的的职责。

sentences.en: The Senate is the most unusual body in the world.
sentences.zh: 参议院是世界上最不寻常的机构。

sentences.en: Our framers designed it to be that way, and it was ingrained in me.
sentences.zh: 我们的制宪先贤将其设计成这样，这已经深深印在我的骨子里。

sentences.en: The filibuster is the only thing.
sentences.zh: 阻挠议事是唯一的东西。

sentences.en: It's the holy grail of keeping us talking and working and becoming friends.
sentences.zh: 这是让我们保持对话、工作并成为朋友的无上法宝。

sentences.en: Jeff being on the Republican side, Tina and I at the time on the Democrat side, but we were all friends because we wanted to get things done.
sentences.zh: 杰夫在共和党那边，蒂娜和我当时在民主党那边，但我们都是朋友，因为我们想把事情办成。

sentences.en: And we knew the Senate was the place to do it.
sentences.zh: 我们知道参议院就是实现这一点的地方。

sentences.en: And they've abdicated that type of responsibilities.
sentences.zh: 而他们却放弃了这种职责。

sentences.en: I mean, those are all pretty bleak words, I think.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些都是相当黯淡的词汇。

sentences.en: You want to call them cowards?
sentences.zh: 你想叫他们懦夫吗？

sentences.en: What do you want to say, Lou?
sentences.zh: 你想说些什么，露露？

sentences.en: I want you to say what you think.
sentences.zh: 我希望你说出你的真实想法。

sentences.en: Pretty straightforward responses here, it seeMs.
sentences.zh: 看来这里的回答相当直截了当。

sentences.en: Yeah, those are pretty straightforward responses and not terribly optimistic.
sentences.zh: 是的，这些回答相当直截了当，而且一点也不乐观。

sentences.en: Senator Flake, when you left the Senate, you had been serving in Congress for 18 years, first as a representative.
sentences.zh: 弗雷克参议员，当你离开参议院时，你已经在国会服务了18年，最初是一名众议员。

sentences.en: In a speech you gave on the floor, you gave this warning, and I'm going to quote here,
sentences.zh: 你在议事大厅发表的演讲中发出了这样的警告，我在这里引用一下：

sentences.en: Let us recognize, as authoritarianism reasserts itself in country after country, that we are by no means immune.
sentences.zh: 让我们认识到，随着独裁统治在许多国家卷土重来，我们绝非百毒不侵。

sentences.en: Do you think you were right to be concerned?
sentences.zh: 你认为你的担忧是正确的吗？

sentences.en: Yes, most definitely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: I'm not saying that we're under an authoritarian system now.
sentences.zh: 我并不是说我们现在处于独裁体制之下。

sentences.en: We're not.
sentences.zh: 我们没有。

sentences.en: But that tendency, and certainly Congress has abdicated its responsibility on a number of areas,
sentences.zh: 但这种倾向，而且国会在很多领域确实放弃了它的责任，

sentences.en: whether it's war powers, whether it's tariffs, issues that rightly belong in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 无论是战争权力、关税，还是理应属于参议院的问题。

sentences.en: And senators have typically, over time, jealously guarded their prerogative.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，参议员们通常会极力捍卫自己的特权。

sentences.en: But they have willingly kind of given that up.
sentences.zh: 但他们却心甘情愿地放弃了这一点。

sentences.en: And you have a president who is eager to take just about everything he can get.
sentences.zh: 而你却有一个急于夺取他能抓到的一切权力的总统。

sentences.en: Now, every president, Republican and Democrat, will push some limits somewhere in terms of executive orders.
sentences.zh: 现在，历任总统，无论是共和党还是民主党，都会在行政命令方面突破某些界限。

sentences.en: This president is doing that in spades, obviously.
sentences.zh: 显然，这位总统在这方面更是有过之而无不及。

sentences.en: But that's why you need a Senate willing to stand up.
sentences.zh: 但这就是为什么你需要一个愿意挺身而出的参议院。

sentences.en: And we've seen inklings lately that you might see some of that coming.
sentences.zh: 我们最近看到了一些迹象，表明你可能会看到其中的一些情况发生。

sentences.en: But, boy, it's been long in coming.
sentences.zh: 但是，天哪，这等得太久了。

sentences.en: And I was concerned then.
sentences.zh: 我当时就很担心。

sentences.en: I'm more concerned today.
sentences.zh: 我今天更加担心了。

sentences.en: Senator, I mentioned just before you left the Senate, you turned away from the Democrats.
sentences.zh: 参议员，我提到就在你离开参议院之前，你退出了民主党。

sentences.en: You registered as an independent.
sentences.zh: 你注册成为了无党派人士。

sentences.en: And in some of your final words, you called the Democratic brand toxic.
sentences.zh: 在你最后的临别之言中，你称民主党的品牌有毒。

sentences.en: Have you seen anything lately that has changed your mind on the direction of the Democratic Party?
sentences.zh: 你最近有没有看到什么改变了你对民主党发展方向看法的改变？

sentences.en: Well, first of all, my state's an R-40 state.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，我的州是一个40%注册为共和党的州。

sentences.en: There's not a redder state than mine.
sentences.zh: 没有比我的州更红的州了。

sentences.en: And it got to the point where the people in West Virginia, when you have a total working class people coming from the lower echelon of the financial rung, okay, hardworking,
sentences.zh: 情况发展到这种地步，西弗吉尼亚州的人民，当你有完全属于来自财务阶梯底层的工薪阶层人民时，好吧，他们是努力工作、

sentences.en: poor people.
sentences.zh: 贫穷的人民。

sentences.en: Why did they all leave the Democrat Party?
sentences.zh: 为什么他们都离开了民主党？

sentences.en: It just kind of left them behind.
sentences.zh: 它只是把他们抛在了后面。

sentences.en: And really, if you want to know, the underlying motive was that a lot of these people would tell me.
sentences.zh: 说实话，如果你想知道的话，潜在的动机是许多这样的人会告诉我。

sentences.en: They said, Joe, listen, the Washington Democratic Party basically has spent more effort, resources, and time for able-bodied, capable people that should be working,
sentences.zh: 他们说，乔，听着，华盛顿民主党基本上花了更多的精力、资源和时间去照顾那些身强力壮、有能力工作却不工作或不愿工作的人，

sentences.en: that don't work or won't work, than those of us who do.
sentences.zh: 而不是照顾我们这些真正在工作的人。

sentences.en: And I've had enough.
sentences.zh: 我已经受够了。

sentences.en: I can't go home and explain what we're doing as far as a Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 我没法回家向选民解释我们在民主党内所做的事情。

sentences.en: So people that are still Democrats in my state, I just says, you better make sure they understand you're an independent West Virginia Democrat.
sentences.zh: 所以我对我们州那些仍然是民主党人的说，你们最好确保别人明白你们是西弗吉尼亚的独立民主党人。

sentences.en: Because if you get tagged as a Washington Democrat, you're underwater 15, 20 points before you start.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你被贴上华盛顿民主党的标签，你在开局前就落后了15到20个百分点。

sentences.en: I mean, that's a warning to the party, for sure.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这绝对是对该党的一个警告。

sentences.en: I try to be as nice as I can, I try to be as truthful as I can, because in some states, some blue and really blue areas, they still can survive and still have a strong, you know,
sentences.zh: 我尽量表现得友好，我尽量保持真实，因为在某些州，一些深蓝甚至极其深蓝的地区，他们仍然可以生存并且拥有强大的，你知道的，

sentences.en: New York City and different places like that may be still strong.
sentences.zh: 纽约市和诸如此类的地方可能依然很强大。

sentences.en: But I can tell you, if you want to know why, you'll never be in the majority again, because you're losing most of the working rural areas.
sentences.zh: 但我可以告诉你，如果你想知道为什么你们将永远无法再次成为多数党，那是因为你们正在失去绝大多数的工薪阶层农村地区。

sentences.en: And that is what has happened.
sentences.zh: 这就是所发生的事情。

sentences.en: All right, Senator Smith, I'm going to turn to you, because you've said you're stepping down to spend more time with family, and that it has nothing to do with politics.
sentences.zh: 好的，史密斯参议员，我要转向你，因为你说你卸任是为了花更多时间陪伴家人，而且这与政治无关。

sentences.en: A lot of politicians who leave say that.
sentences.zh: 很多离职的政客都这么说。

sentences.en: That is the classic line.
sentences.zh: 那是经典说辞。

sentences.en: Come on, tell us the truth.
sentences.zh: 得了吧，告诉我们实话吧。

sentences.en: When I say I want to spend more time with my family, I actually mean it because I really like my family.
sentences.zh: 当我说我想花更多时间陪伴家人时，我是认真的，因为我真的很喜欢我的家人。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: But I've also said a few other things about why I'm leaving.
sentences.zh: 但我还说过关于我为什么要离开的其他一些事情。

sentences.en: Yeah, whenever you leave a job, it can be for personal reasons, but there's always professional reasons.
sentences.zh: 是的，无论什么时候你离开一份工作，可能出于个人原因，但也总有职业原因。

sentences.en: I noted that Representative Jared Golden, who is also stepping down from the House,
sentences.zh: 我注意到同样要辞去众议员职务的贾雷德·戈登，

sentences.en: he talked about political nastiness and the political violence that we're seeing for reasons that he's not seeking re-election.
sentences.zh: 他谈到了政治恶臭以及我们所看到的政治暴力，这些是他不再寻求连任的原因。

sentences.en: So I'm just wondering, are those issues weighing on you, too?
sentences.zh: 所以我很好奇，这些问题也在困扰着你吗？

sentences.en: You know, I made the decision not to run for re-election, you know, in December, January of 2024, 2025.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我是在2024、2025年12月、1杰月做出不参加连任竞选的决定的。

sentences.en: And then everything that has happened this year has certainly not made me wonder whether I made the right decision.
sentences.zh: 然后今年发生的一切当然没有让我怀疑自己是否做出了正确的决定。

sentences.en: I mean, I had, you know, this horrible political assassination of my dear friend Melissa Hortman, the Speaker of the Emerita of the Minnesota House.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，发生了我亲爱的朋友、明尼苏达州众议院前议长梅利莎·霍特曼遭遇的这起可怕的政治暗杀事件。

sentences.en: We had the shooting of the Annunciation School, which is literally 10 blocks from where I live.
sentences.zh: 我们还经历了圣母领报学校的枪击案，该校离我住的地方只有十个街区。

sentences.en: And so the reality of these political attacks, and of course, in this moment, fueled by the President of the United States,
sentences.zh: 因此，这些政治攻击的现实，当然在此时此刻，是由美国总统推波助澜的，

sentences.en: who just a couple of weeks ago said that two of my colleagues and four members of the House of Representatives should be tried for treason and executed.
sentences.zh: 他就在几周前说，我的两位同僚和四名众议院议员应该因叛国罪受审并被处决。

sentences.en: Of course, these things all have impact.
sentences.zh: 当然，这些事情都会产生影响。

sentences.en: But, you know, there was another part of it for me, which is that I'm going to – I'm what is my 68, roughly?
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，对我和说还有另一部分原因，那就是我将要——我大概是68岁左右？

sentences.en: I will be 68 next year.
sentences.zh: 我明年将满68岁。

sentences.en: Pretty young for a Democratic senator.
sentences.zh: 对于民主党参议员来说算很年轻了。

sentences.en: Yes, it is.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: Yes, it is.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: She's on the low end of the spectrum right there.
sentences.zh: 她在那里面处于较低的年龄段。

sentences.en: And, you know, I am not burdened by the belief that I am the only one who can do this job.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我没有那种认为只有我才能胜任这项工作的执念。

sentences.en: I feel really confident in the bench that is there in Minnesota to carry on, and I'm actually quite invigorated by making space for those leaders to step in.
sentences.zh: 我对明尼苏达州能够接替这一职位的后备人才充满信心，而且为这些领导人腾出空间让我感到非常振奋。

sentences.en: When I left, I didn't – I never said I want to spend more time with family.
sentences.zh: 当我离开时，我没有——我从来没说过我想花更多时间陪家人。

sentences.en: I love my family, but I would have liked to have served another term.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的家人，但我其实想再干一个任期。

sentences.en: I mean, you don't get all the way to the most exclusive club in the world and just want to stay one term.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你历经艰险进入了世界上最排外的俱乐部，不会只想呆一个任期。

sentences.en: So I would have liked to, but the price for doing so would have been –
sentences.zh: 所以我本想继续，但这样做的代价将是——

sentences.en: Yeah, I know what you mean.
sentences.zh: 是的，我明白你的意思。

sentences.en: Yeah, it would have been for me to say, you know, those principles I said I believed in, I no longer do.
sentences.zh: 是的，那对我来说意味着去说，你知道，我曾经信仰的那些原则，我不再信仰了。

sentences.en: And that – the cost, the price for that was too steep to pay.
sentences.zh: 而那——为此付出的代价太沉重了。

sentences.en: Those of us who have been in these tough races before, when you're facing something, you know what's going to turn you into a different animal than you're not.
sentences.zh: 我们这些以前参加过这些艰难竞选的人，当你面临某些事情时，你知道那会把你变成一个你本不是的不同动物。

sentences.en: It's not – I know you, and I know Tim.
sentences.zh: 这不是——我了解你，我也了解蒂姆。

sentences.en: That's not who we are, I don't think.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们不是那样的人。

sentences.en: But we'd have had to turn into another animal if we wanted to go on.
sentences.zh: 但如果我们想继续下去，我们就不得不变成另一种动物。

sentences.en: I've never faced an election where I thought the other side was the enemy.
sentences.zh: 我从未经历过这样一场选举，在选举中我认为对方是敌人。

sentences.en: I learned from every election I was in a debate, and after the election was over, I won most of them.
sentences.zh: 我从我参加过的每一场辩论选举中学习，选举结束后，我赢了其中大多数。

sentences.en: So I'd call the person.
sentences.zh: 所以我打电话给那个人。

sentences.en: I said, you know, you have some good ideas in that debate.
sentences.zh: 我说，你知道，你在那场辩论中有些好主意。

sentences.en: I said, can we talk about that and start building relationships?
sentences.zh: 我说，我们能谈谈那个并开始建立关系吗？

sentences.en: That's gone.
sentences.zh: 这已经不复存在了。

sentences.en: I'll say that's not in vogue now, but I don't think it's gone.
sentences.zh: 我会说现在这不流行了，但我认为它并没有消失。

sentences.en: I think it can return.
sentences.zh: 我认为它是可以回来的。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I don't think it's gone either.
sentences.zh: 我也不认为它已经消失了。

sentences.en: And I haven't given up hope on that, Joe.
sentences.zh: 而且我对那个并没有放弃希望，乔。

sentences.en: I believe that it's still there.
sentences.zh: 我坚信它仍然存在。

sentences.en: I never give up, but I'm just dealing with reality today.
sentences.zh: 我从不放弃，但我今天只是在面对现实。

sentences.en: The thing that I see, Jeff, and you can talk about this, you came from the House.
sentences.zh: 杰夫，我看到的情况是，而且你可以谈谈这个，你曾来自众议院。

sentences.en: I came from being a governor, which is the most collegial of all institutions.
sentences.zh: 我曾担任州长，这是所有体制中最具同事精神的。

sentences.en: You can go to a governor's National Governors Association.
sentences.zh: 你可以去全国州长协会了解。

sentences.en: If I didn't know that that person was a Republican, you could not tell the difference.
sentences.zh: 如果我不知道那个人是共和党人，你根本分不出来。

sentences.en: We're all working for the same – curing the same probleMs.
sentences.zh: 我们都在为同一个目标努力——解决相同的问题。

sentences.en: The House, you all operate on simple majority 218, okay?
sentences.zh: 在众议院，你们所有人都靠简单多数的218票运作，对吧？

sentences.en: Don't even have to acknowledge the other side.
sentences.zh: 甚至不需要理会另一方。

sentences.en: Don't even have to let them be involved if you don't want to, okay?
sentences.zh: 如果你不想的话，甚至不需要让他们参与，对吧？

sentences.en: I kept noticing more and more Congress people that kept coming to the Senate with that mindset made it harder for the Senate to stay collegiate.
sentences.zh: 我不断注意到越来越多的国会议员带着这种心态来到参议院，这使得参议院更难保持同僚精神。

sentences.en: Oh, definitely.
sentences.zh: 哦，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: Am I right?
sentences.zh: 我说得对吗？

sentences.en: Yes, completely.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: I mean, the real turn in the House came 2005, 2006.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，众议院真正的转折点发生在2005年、2006年。

sentences.en: I got there in 2001 when we didn't adopt formally, but basically lived by the so-called Hastert rule.
sentences.zh: 我是在2001年进入国会的，当时我们虽然没有正式采纳，但基本上遵循了所谓的“哈斯特规则”。

sentences.en: And it wasn't Hastert, it was really Tom DeLay and a few others who basically said,
sentences.zh: 而且这并不是哈斯特本人提出的，实际上是汤姆·迪雷和其他几个人，他们基本上说：

sentences.en: if you're going to bring something to the floor as a Republican, and we had a bigger cushion at that time
sentences.zh: 如果你作为共和党人要把某项法案提交到全院表决，而且我们当时有更大的缓冲余地，

sentences.en: in the majority, but that you should be able to pass it just with Republican votes.
sentences.zh: 在多数席位中，你应该仅凭共和党人的选票就能通过它。

sentences.en: And if it might gather bipartisan support, then, you know, knock some provisions off so it won't be attractive.
sentences.zh: 如果它可能会获得两党支持，那么，你知道，就把一些条款去掉，这样它就不会那么吸引人了。

sentences.en: And then you use that as a cudgel during the next election.
sentences.zh: 然后你在下次选举中把它当作大棒来挥舞。

sentences.en: And that, you know, you had people kind of mature as politicians, I guess, under that system.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在这种系统下，有些人在政治上成熟了，我猜是这样的。

sentences.en: And some of them have gone to the Senate.
sentences.zh: 其中有些人已经进入了参议院。

sentences.en: I mean, this is what Mitch McConnell said, like, my purpose is to beat Obama.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是米奇·麦康奈尔所说的，比如，我的目标就是击败奥巴马。

sentences.en: And gradually, the partisanship just ramped up.
sentences.zh: 渐渐地，党派偏见就这样升级了。

sentences.en: You know, it's funny listening to you all, and it's one of the reasons I wanted to bring you here, because you have the long view of how we got here.
sentences.zh: 你知道，听你们大家讲话很有意思，这也是我想把你们请到这里的原因之一，因为你们对我们是如何走到这一步有着长远的眼光。

sentences.en: And clearly, all of this predates the era that we're in now.
sentences.zh: 很显然，这一切都发生在我们现在所处的时代之前。

sentences.en: But this era has supercharged all of what you're discussing.
sentences.zh: 但这个时代给你们正在讨论的所有事情都加了码。

sentences.en: And you've touched on one of the main critiques of the Senate right now.
sentences.zh: 你们也触及了目前对参议院的主要批评之一。

sentences.en: And it's something I heard when I sat with Senator Lisa Murkowski, which is that the Senate is now, regardless of the partisan nature, it's just not doing its job.
sentences.zh: 这是我与参议员丽莎·穆尔科斯基坐在一起时听到的，也就是参议院现在，无论党派性质如何，它就是没有在履行职责。

sentences.en: It's not acting as a check on the executive.
sentences.zh: 它没有起到对行政部门的制衡作用。

sentences.en: And I would love for you to just discuss, do you think that this is an enduring shift away from congressional power?
sentences.zh: 我很想听听你们的讨论，你们认为这是一个对国会权力进行持久削弱的转变吗？

sentences.en: I don't think it's an enduring condition.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这是一个持久的状况。

sentences.en: I think it has to do with leadership.
sentences.zh: 我认为这与领导层有关。

sentences.en: I look at the potential field on the Democratic and Republican side, and you see some who will try to, you know, replicate what President Trump has done in terms of amassing power
sentences.zh: 我看了看民主党和共和党阵营的潜在人选，你会发现有些人会试图，你知道，复制特朗普总统在权力集中方面所做的事情，

sentences.en: and kind of stiffing the House and the Senate.
sentences.zh: 并且有点架空众议院和参议院。

sentences.en: But the vast majority of Republican senators, who I'm most familiar with, don't like this at all.
sentences.zh: 但绝大多数我最熟悉的共和党参议员一点也不喜欢这样。

sentences.en: They want to reassert their prerogatives.
sentences.zh: 他们希望重新声张自己的特权。

sentences.en: They know that the Senate, you know, has the reputation of being the world's most deliberative body, and they'd like to get back to deliberating.
sentences.zh: 他们知道参议院享有世界上最具审议性质机构的美誉，他们希望回到审议的正轨上来。

sentences.en: So I do think that this isn't a condition that has to stay.
sentences.zh: 所以我确实认为这并非一种必须保持下去的现状。

sentences.en: But we've never seen a time when presidential powers have been given back.
sentences.zh: 但我们从未见过总统权力被收回的时期。

sentences.en: The president, as I was saying before— the Supreme Court ruling on this and sort of making it law, essentially.
sentences.zh: 正如我刚才所说，总统——最高法院对此作出了裁决，并基本上将其确立为法律。

sentences.en: Yeah, but the president has amassed far more power and is using far more power than the Supreme Court has granted him now.
sentences.zh: 是的，但是总统集聚了更多的权力，并且正在使用比最高法院现在授予他的更多的权力。

sentences.en: But it's not been codified.
sentences.zh: 但这还没有被法典化。

sentences.en: And, yeah.
sentences.zh: 而且，是的。

sentences.en: Not yet.
sentences.zh: 还没有。

sentences.en: So you'll—
sentences.zh: 所以你会——

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think it's—you know, my sense of it is that I completely agree with Jeff that behind the scenes you will hear many Republicans in the Senate say,
sentences.zh: 我认为——你知道，我的感觉是，我完全同意杰夫的看法，在幕后你会听到参议院的许多共和党人说：

sentences.en: I don't like this.
sentences.zh: 我不喜欢这样。

sentences.en: I don't think this is right.
sentences.zh: 我认为这不对。

sentences.en: But then they also say, we're just waiting for the right moment.
sentences.zh: 但随后他们也会说，我们只是在等待合适的时机。

sentences.en: We're waiting for the right moment to actually do something about it.
sentences.zh: 我们在等待合适的时机真正采取行动。

sentences.en: And meanwhile, the powers of the Senate and the powers of the legislative branch are— I mean, they're gushing out of the Capitol.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，参议院的权力和立法部门的权力正在——我的意思是，它们正从国会大厦里大量流失。

sentences.en: I mean, and it's not just the Senate.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，不只是参议院。

sentences.en: I mean, what the Speaker did to keep the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，议长为了让美国

sentences.en: House of Representatives out of session for—how many days was it?
sentences.zh: 众议院休会——那是多少天？

sentences.en: Seven weeks.
sentences.zh: 七周。

sentences.en: You know, seven weeks was really an incredible abdication of responsibility and authority.
sentences.zh: 你知道，七周真的是对责任和权威令人难以置信的放弃。

sentences.en: So it's interesting to me because I'm always so fascinated by the interpersonal relationships of everybody in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 所以这对我来说很有趣，因为我总是对参议院里每个的人际关系着迷。

sentences.en: And the people that I see that seem to feel the most betrayed right now are my Democratic colleagues who stake their careers on working across party lines to accomplish things.
sentences.zh: 而我看到的那些现在似乎感到最被背叛的人，是我的民主党同僚，他们把自己的职业生涯押在跨越党派界限来完成事情上。

sentences.en: They were part of the gangs.
sentences.zh: 他们曾是跨党派小组成员。

sentences.en: They were in the—you know, so much of the work that you did, Joe, around the Infrastructure
sentences.zh: 他们身处其中——你知道，乔，你围绕《基础设施法》做了那么多工作，

sentences.en: Act, and they feel as if the bonds of trust between Democrats and Republicans have been
sentences.zh: 他们觉得民主党和共和党之间的信任纽带已经彻底破裂，

sentences.en: so broken because of the ways in which Republicans in the Senate have just basically kowtowed to
sentences.zh: 因为参议院的共和党人基本上对总统卑躬屈膝，

sentences.en: the president, not only on the, you know, on the fact of basically allowing him to undo our budget bills, but, I mean, on the ways that they have kind of confirmed against their
sentences.zh: 不仅在事实上允许他废除我们的预算案，而且我认为，在他们违背更好判断力去确认其中一些真正糟糕的提名人的方面，比如小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪

sentences.en: better judgment, I would argue, some of these really terrible nominees like RFK Jr.
sentences.zh: 和国防部长这样的提名人。

sentences.en: and like the Secretary of Defense.
sentences.zh: 所以部分问题在于，我相信，这也是我认为我和乔有分歧的地方。

sentences.en: So part of the problem, I believe, this is where I think Joe and I differ.
sentences.zh: 也许我和这里的所有同僚都有分歧。

sentences.en: Maybe I differ from both of my colleagues here.
sentences.zh: 我认为参议院的规则彻底阻碍了参议院做任何事情的能力。

sentences.en: I think that the Senate rules have so completely stymied the ability of the Senate to do anything.
sentences.zh: 我指的不仅仅是阻挠议事（长篇辩论）。

sentences.en: And I'm not just talking about the filibuster.
sentences.zh: 我认为必须找到一种方法来让参议院的系统运转得更好。

sentences.en: I think there's got to be a way of figuring out how to make the systems of the Senate work better.
sentences.zh: 因为你想废除阻挠议事。

sentences.en: Because you'd like to get rid of the filibuster.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我至少希望改革它，这样如果你要阻挠一项法案，你至少得站在该死的议会大厅里发表讲话。

sentences.en: I mean, I would at least like to reform it so that if you're going to filibuster a bill, you ought to at least have to stand on the damn floor and talk.
sentences.zh: 我们在这一点上完全一致。

sentences.en: And we're exactly alike on that.
sentences.zh: 而不是只说，哦，我不喜欢这个，所以我要反对，然后，你知道，出去吃晚饭。

sentences.en: Instead of just saying, oh, I don't like this, so I'm going to object and then, you know, go out for dinner.
sentences.zh: 任何拥有多数席位的总统都会想要废除阻挠议事。

sentences.en: Every president who has a majority is going to want to get rid of the filibuster.
sentences.zh: 而每一届参议院都应该抵制这一点。

sentences.en: And every Senate ought to resist that.
sentences.zh: 彻底抵制它。

sentences.en: Totally resist it.
sentences.zh: 无论是共和党人还是民主党人，因为它是仅存的少数几个迫使人们共同合作的机制之一。

sentences.en: Republican or Democrat, because it is one of the few mechanisms left that forces people to work together.
sentences.zh: 我在过去八年里一直在观察参议院，我没有看到阻挠议事是治愈党派偏见的灵丹妙药。

sentences.en: I've watched the Senate for the last eight years, and I have not seen that the filibuster is the pill to cure partisanship.
sentences.zh: 我看到的是，党派偏见是——我的意思是，有时寻求60票多数的需求确实会促成像《基础设施和就业法》这样强有力的立法。

sentences.en: What I see is that partisanship is, I mean, sometimes certainly the need to find a 60 vote majority creates strong pieces of legislation like the Infrastructure and Jobs Act.
sentences.zh: 但有时它恰恰造成了那些让美国人想要完成的事情很难真正完成的制度。

sentences.en: But sometimes it creates the very systems that make it very difficult for the things that Americans want to get done to actually get done.
sentences.zh: 我想回到这个话题。

sentences.en: I want to come back to this.
sentences.zh: 但在我们这样做之前，我对政党领导层的问题很好奇。

sentences.en: But before we do, I am curious about the problem of party leadership.
sentences.zh: 例如，参议院少数党领袖查克·舒默并不受民主党基层欢迎，

sentences.en: For example, Senator Chuck Schumer, the Senate minority leader, isn't popular with the Democratic
sentences.zh: 而史密斯参议员，你是寻求新领导层的所谓“战斗俱乐部”的一员。

sentences.en: base, and Senator Smith, you are part of a so-called fight club that is looking to get new leadership.
sentences.zh: 你能解释一下你认为需要什么吗？

sentences.en: Can you explain what you think is needed?
sentences.zh: 各政党的领导层是否也是导致这一切的原因之一？

sentences.en: And is the leadership of the respective parties part of what's going on here?
sentences.zh: 嗯，在一个正常运转的立法机构中，你会认为民主党领袖和共和党领袖会一直互相交流，对吧，试图弄清楚

sentences.en: Well, so in a functioning legislative body, you would think that the Democratic leader and the Republican leader would talk to each other all the time, right, to try to figure
sentences.zh: 事情，试图让事情运转起来。

sentences.en: things out, try to get things going.
sentences.zh: 参议院的党派偏见程度已经达到了这种地步，以至于这种事情再也不会发生了。

sentences.en: The level of partisanship in the Senate is at such a degree that it just doesn't happen anymore.
sentences.zh: 我所属的这个非正式团体，是一群对领袖在决定哪些候选人在哪些州参选时的做法感到抱怨和不满的参议员，

sentences.en: The informal group that I am a part of, it's a group of senators who have been complaining
sentences.zh: 这主要是关于那个，有点像民主党参议院竞选委员会（DSCC）的工作选举如何。

sentences.en: and unhappy primarily with the ways in which the leader has been identifying what candidates he wants to run in what states.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣，因为当我与舒默参议员交谈时，他把这吹嘘为他最大的优势，即他真的能挑选出能赢得选举的候选人。

sentences.en: It has been primarily about that, kind of like how the elections of the work of the DSCC
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，你会让77岁的珍妮特·米尔斯州长在缅因州与41岁且更具进步色彩的格雷厄姆·普拉特纳竞选。

sentences.en: Which is interesting, because when I spoke to Senator Schumer, he touted that as his greatest sort of strength, that he really can choose candidates that win.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这就引发了一场党内斗争。

sentences.en: And so, you know, you get a Governor Janet Mills running in Maine at 77 against Graham Plattner, who's 41 and more progressive.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为确实如此。

sentences.en: And so, you know, that sets up an intraparty fight.
sentences.zh: 澄清一下，我没有在缅因州支持任何人，但我在明尼苏达州也还没有支持任何人，因为我认为这应该由选民来决定。

sentences.en: Yes, I think it does.
sentences.zh: 我在缅因州支持苏珊·柯林斯。

sentences.en: To be clear, I haven't endorsed anybody in Maine, but I haven't endorsed anybody in Minnesota yet either, because I think that it should be up to the voters to decide.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: I'm endorsing Susan Collins in Maine.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 如果你除掉了苏珊·柯林斯，那么你真的就失去了参议院。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 持有这种心态的人，我们甚至无法让他们再参选了。

sentences.en: If you get rid of a Susan Collins, then you're really losing the Senate.
sentences.zh: 中间派的好人。

sentences.en: People that have that mindset, we can't even get them to run anymore.
sentences.zh: 如果你看看参议院，你提到了查克·舒默，有些人会看着他们

sentences.en: Good people in the middle.
sentences.zh: 说他们太具党派色彩，什么事也做不成，他们永远不会跨越党派分歧。

sentences.en: If you look in the Senate, and you mentioned Chuck Schumer, and some people will look at them
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们过去曾这样做过。

sentences.en: and say they're too partisan to get anything done, they won't ever reach across the aisle.
sentences.zh: 我曾与查克·舒默和迪克·德宾一起成为“八人帮”的一员。

sentences.en: Well, they have in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 移民之战。

sentences.en: I was part of the Gang of Eight with Chuck Schumer and Dick Durbin.
sentences.zh: 是的，关于移民问题。

sentences.en: The Immigration War.
sentences.zh: 我们以68票对32票通过了一项法案。

sentences.en: Yes, on immigration.
sentences.zh: 那是我们看到的参议院按其以往方式运作的最后几个例子之一。

sentences.en: We passed a bill of 68 to 32.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们现在看着并说他们绝不会这样做的某些相同人物，

sentences.en: That was one of the last examples we've seen of the Senate working how it used to work.
sentences.zh: 他们能做到，而且过去也做到过，但现在的激励机制严重错位了。

sentences.en: My point is, some of the same characters that we now look at and say, they could never do this.

sentences.zh: 就像是，你在政治光谱中属于哪一类？

sentences.zh: 我其实觉得这根本不是正确的政治光谱划分。

sentences.zh: 让我来谈谈这种两党合作梦想的反面观点，

sentences.en: which is, did we get here perhaps because the Senate's been ineffective at responding to the real problems that voters have because it's incremental?
sentences.zh: 那就是，我们走到这一步，会不会是因为参议院在应对选民面临的实际问题时一直毫无效率，因为它总是采用渐进主义？

sentences.en: There's just not any big swings anymore.
sentences.zh: 现在根本没有什么大的动作了。

sentences.en: I mean, people at the moment seem to be clamoring for these ideas that can solve their very real probleMs.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当下的人们似乎在强烈呼吁那些能够解决他们切身问题的理念。

sentences.en: Does incrementalism, which can read as bipartisanship, actually get the job done at a moment like this?
sentences.zh: 可以被解读为两党合作的渐进主义，在这样的时刻真的能把事情办成吗？

sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为这正是问题的关键所在。

sentences.en: If you look at Americans over the last probably, what,
sentences.zh: 如果你看看过去差不多，什么，

sentences.en: 20, 30 years, significant majorities of Americans have said that they think that things are terribly on the wrong track, that they're working as hard as they possibly can,
sentences.zh: 20、30年来的美国人，相当多数的美国人一直表示，他们认为事情严重走向了错误的方向，他们已经尽其所能地努力工作了，

sentences.en: and nothing is really changing.
sentences.zh: 但实际上没有任何改变。

sentences.en: And so, like, if you have a governing body that isn't capable, hasn't been capable of making the big changes that need to be made, of course people are going to be frustrated.

sentences.en: And what I think is so interesting, because we often kind of get sucked into this sort of, is this, you know, are you moderate?

sentences.en: I actually don't think that's the right continuum at all.
sentences.zh: 我其实觉得这根本不是正确的政治光谱划分。

sentences.en: I think it's a question of whether you actually think that the status quo was pretty much working, whether you think that it needs to be fundamentally changed.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个问题：你究竟是认为现状基本上运作良好，还是认为它需要根本性的改变。

sentences.en: And Americans are telling us that the status quo is not working for them.
sentences.zh: 而美国人在告诉我们，现状对他们来说行不通。

sentences.en: And they're telling us that things that maybe would be seen as being, like, progressive, it's actually, like, 75% issues, paid family and medical leave,

sentences.en: So all of that argues to me that we need a body, a Senate and a Congress that's capable of making those kinds of big changes.
sentences.zh: 因此，所有这些都在向我说明，我们需要一个有能力做出那种重大改变的机构——一个参议院和国会。

sentences.en: Well, I make the case for incrementalism.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我来为渐进主义辩护。

sentences.zh: 而参议院随着时间的推移一直是行之有效的。

sentences.zh: 比如说，
